definitions.explanation: The area or ground immediately around or beneath one's feet.
The stability or condition of one's stance.
Figuratively, a vulnerability that can be exploited.

examples.japanese: {足元|あしもと}に{気|き}をつけてください。
{暗|くら}いから{足元|あしもと}が{見|み}えない。
examples.english: It's dark, so I can't see where I'm stepping.

examples.japanese: {足元|あしもと}を{見|み}られている。
examples.english: They're taking advantage of my weakness.

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}が{足元|あしもと}にすり{寄|よ}ってきた。
examples.english: The cat rubbed against my feet.

examples.japanese: {足元|あしもと}に{水|みず}たまりがあった。
examples.english: There was a puddle at my feet.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}で{足元|あしもと}が{滑|すべ}りやすい。
examples.english: The ground is slippery underfoot because of the rain.

examples.japanese: {酔|よ}って{足元|あしもと}がおぼつかない。
examples.english: Being drunk, I'm unsteady on my feet.

examples.japanese: {足元|あしもと}をしっかり{固|かた}める。
{足元|あしもと}が{定|さだ}まらない。
ボクサーの{足元|あしもと}が{軽|かる}い。
{足元|あしもと}を{狙|ねら}われた。
{彼|かれ}は{足元|あしもと}にも{及|およ}ばない。
examples.english: He doesn't hold a candle to them.

examples.japanese: {タクシー|たくしー}に{足元|あしもと}を{見|み}られた。
examples.english: The taxi driver took advantage of my situation.

examples.japanese: {足元|あしもと}をすくわれないように{注意|ちゅうい}しろ。
examples.english: Be careful not to be caught off guard.

notes:
USAGE: {足元|あしもと} has both literal and figurative meanings.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{足元|あしもと}に{気|き}をつける (to watch one's step)
・{足元|あしもと}がおぼつかない (to be unsteady on one's feet)
・{足元|あしもと}を{見|み}る (to exploit someone's weakness)
・{足元|あしもと}にも{及|およ}ばない (to not hold a candle to; to be far inferior)

WRITING VARIATIONS: Can also be written as {足下|あしもと}.

RELATED:
・{足場|あしば} - foothold, scaffold
・{地面|じめん} - ground
